title: Reading rock layers and geologic history
subject: Earth & space

sources.title: NGSS MS-ESS1-4: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence from rock strata for how the geologic time scale is used to organize Earth's 4.6-billion-year-old history
Earle, Physical Geology 2nd ed. (BCcampus), 8.2 Relative Dating Methods
Earle, Physical Geology 2nd ed. (BCcampus), 3.1 The Rock Cycle

legend.name: Dike
legend.meaning: Dark igneous rock that cooled from magma

steps.title: Layer D
steps.instruction: Trace the bottom layer, on both sides of the gap.

note.text: Sediment settles in flat layers, one on top of another. The bottom layer was laid down first.

steps.title: Layer C
steps.instruction: Trace layer C, on both sides.

note.text: Layer C settled on top of D, so it's younger. This is the principle of superposition.

steps.title: Layer B
steps.instruction: Trace layer B, on both sides.

note.text: Each layer records a time. A change in rock type means the place changed, like a sea becoming a muddy shore.

steps.title: Dike
steps.instruction: Trace the dark band cutting up through the layers.

note.text: A dike is magma that forced its way up through cracks and cooled. It cuts layers B, C and D, so it's younger than them.
Layer A lies over the top of the dike without being cut, so it formed after the dike.

steps.title: Fossils
steps.instruction: Trace the two shell fossils in layer C.

note.text: Fossils are dated by the layer they're in. These shells lived while layer C was forming, before B and A.

steps.title: Tell the story
steps.instruction: Tap the events from oldest to youngest.
items: Layer C is deposited, with shells
Magma cuts through as a dike
Layer A is deposited on top
steps.why: Lower layers are older (superposition), and the dike is younger than the layers it cuts (cross-cutting).

steps.title: Evidence
steps.question: How do we know the dike is older than layer A?

options.text: The dike stops at layer A instead of cutting through it
options.feedback: Yes. Layer A was laid on top after the dike cooled. If the dike were younger, it would cut A too.
Color doesn't show age. What matters is which rock cuts across which.
The dike reaches up through B. What shows it's older than A is that it doesn't cut A.
We can: the dike ends under layer A, so A formed after it.

steps.title: Time scale
steps.question: How do geologists build the geologic time scale of Earth's 4.6-billion-year history?

options.text: By matching the order of rock layers and the fossils in them from place to place
options.feedback: Right. Layers and fossils show which events came first, so Earth's history can be put in order and divided into eras.

options.text: By counting every year since Earth formed
options.feedback: No one could count that. The order of layers and fossils puts events in sequence.
People have written for only a few thousand years. Rocks record far older events.

options.text: By measuring how tall mountains are
options.feedback: Height doesn't give an order of events. Layers and fossils do.
